paragraphs: Friend, this passage is HEAVY, and I won't pretend otherwise. The LORD says the people abandoned Him, chased other gods and filled this place with the blood of the innocent (Jeremiah 19:4). Then He says what they did with their children was something He never commanded or mentioned, "nor did it even enter My mind" (Jeremiah 19:5). Whatever else this passage says, it says God takes the sin and the suffering seriously.

Now look at that jar. Jeremiah smashes it in front of the elders and the priests, and the LORD says He will shatter this nation "like one shatters a potter's jar that can never again be repaired" (Jeremiah 19:11). I think that sound was meant to get through, because words alone weren't landing. The LORD says why in verse 15: "they have stiffened their necks so as not to heed My words." They heard every word and STILL wouldn't turn their heads, and that's the warning for all of us.

So here's what I'm taking from it, baker. When God speaks, listening is only half the job, and the other half is turning toward Him. I know a little about being stuck in the dark, and I can tell you the way out started when I answered the One who called. Today, don't just hear the Word. Let it move you.
